selection.why: This is the cleanest strong plan: median case span falls 2.2281% (z=-4.70), mean case span falls 2.1731% (z=-5.70), and waiting falls 1.8273% (z=-4.63), with no significant worsening and no significant service or utilisation change. It gives up some headline magnitude versus round2c, but avoids its additional covered and worsening candidates.
selection.gain_reading: speed — waiting h/case improves significantly by 1.8273% (z=-4.63), while service h/case rises 4.7979% but is not significant (z=0.77); this supports the computed queueing-speed interpretation rather than a claim that less work was done. The attributable activity changes include -1.4354 h/case for AC-001, -0.0388 for AC-002, and -0.1501 for CBW-002, but those activity hours are not directly comparable with the case-span waiting and service measures.

selection.caveat: Do not over-read the result as a service-time or utilisation improvement: service rose 4.7979% with z=0.77 and utilisation rose 6.7422% with z=1.05, both noise. CBW-003 and CBW-002 are passengers in this measured plan, while CR-001 and CR-002 have log-reported exogenous savings that the simulator does not represent; those savings are evidence outside these simulated columns, not measured case-span gains.

rulings.reason: In this prior judgement of a Dutch bank loan process, lead handling itself does not plausibly carry a specific legal, regulatory, audit, or consumer-protection obligation, though this judgement may be wrong; no_objection is not an endorsement.

compliance_final.asked: every round during the loop, and once more here on the union of everything measured
compliance_final.note: DECISIONS B: judged on prior knowledge alone and never overturnable by measurement. This ruling decides what the deliverable may contain; measurements of plans it bars are kept under `excluded_as_non_compliant` so the cost of the block can still be read.

note: `best` is the best MEASUREMENT in the run, which is usually not the last round. ⚠️ `statistically_tied_with_best` is the SELECTOR'S CANDIDATE POOL, not a set of indistinguishable results: a row is admitted either because it is not significantly worse than `best` on the median, or because it is decisively better on ONE directional measure while possibly far worse on the others. Read each row's `admitted_because` before describing it, and never call the list a tie. `per_candidate` is the winning plan's own account: what each surviving candidate contributed on waiting, duration, throughput and resources.
